_comment: PER-TIER SETTINGS arm: the b4_nows_fanout_cb input (fan-out cuts as switch_chain-only user cuts) plus objective_tier_params. Compare against b4_nows_fanout_cb (remote 2026-11-22: tiers 1-3 368/526/7276 s, tier 3 crossover 7057 s; tier 4 incumbent 964 -> 708 in 14 s, then one unfinished root LP re-solve of 457K simplex iterations for the rest of its 1 h cap, bound 64). Tier 3 Symmetry 0: its time went into crossover from Gurobi's symmetry-reduced LP solution ('Use crossover to convert LP symmetric solution'); Symmetry 0 replaces that path by the ordinary concurrent root LP (checked locally on tier 1). Tier 3 closed at its root in both earlier runs, so losing MIP symmetry handling there should cost little. Tier 4 DegenMoves 0: the post-root simplex stall matches Gurobi's degenerate-moves phase (simplex pivots across a degenerate optimal face to make the root solution more integral); 0 skips it, so the cut loop and the fan-out user cuts get to run. Tier 4 NoRelHeurTime 300: 5 min of the no-relaxation heuristic before the root LP, since every earlier tier-4 improvement came from heuristics in the first 14 s. What to compare: tier 3 time and crossover time; in tier 4 whether the node log moves past the root, the 'User: N' line and the printed 'fan-out user cuts' line (also in this log), the bound (64 before), NoRel solutions, and the final switch_chain value (708 / 726 before). Hierarchical MILP AllGather on rail_optimized_256gpu_dual_plane with switch copy. 256-GPU rail-optimized dual-plane fabric. Every GPU has a port into both planes, so every host transit is co-located (forward dwell 1). Hierarchical only. milp_chunking=4: one MILP chunk = 4 of a host's 8 identities for one destination-cell set, so 2 chunks per host -- between 'holder' (8, intractable here) and 'cell' (1, voids multipath across the 8 uplinks). Bundles span holder GPUs, so three GPUs of each group of four stage through the NVSwitch. switch_copy [true, false]: the network switches of the coarse level copy -- a fan-out is one Send, charged once on its uplink, and ncclize emits it as ONE multicast send threadblock (tb send="r1,r2") with one mscclflowid, plus a switch-JSON (format 2) entry listing every out port; the cell NVSwitches do not copy (multicast there needs NVLS). Pass --no-multicast to ncclize for the pre-multicast output (one unicast send per branch). SLOWEST_LINK keeps every coarse link at >= 1 chunk/epoch (occupancy 1: no multi-epoch legs). objective_type 6 (LEXICOGRAPHIC) puts makespan first; PAPER (3) ties on it. Outputs: Schedules/<prefix>_flat.json (+ _coarse/_identities/_intra side outputs). The fan-out-cut arm: the b4_nows_nodrop input plus switch_fanout_cuts, so compare it against that run (2026-11-15: makespan 398 s, latency 553 s, host_relay 7318 s of which 7097 s crossover, switch_chain root bound 64, incumbent 964 -> 726 in its first 32 s and no change after, 6 h limit). switch_fanout_cuts true adds one row per (leaf, epoch), deliveries <= entries + 30 (F = 31 hosts one chunk can reach, m = 32 downlinks): valid for every integer schedule, so no optimum moves, but the LP relaxation can no longer fill a leaf with ~1.03 entries made of slivers. Expect the switch_chain root bound ('Root relaxation: objective ...' in that tier) near 118 instead of 64; the true optimum is between 119 and 124. What to compare: that bound, the incumbent trajectory of the tier, the final value, and the time of tiers 1-3 (the rows are present there too but should be slack). objective_tier_time_limit [null, null, null, 1.0] caps switch_chain at 1 h: the other run made all of its progress in its first minute, so its value at 1 h equals its final 726. num_epochs 8 IS the ingress bound (62 chunks into 8 in-links of 1 chunk/epoch), so no horizon past it can help; the leaf broadcast (2 columns per cell over 8 leaves) also takes 8, and the 2026-11-10 dual-plane b4_nows run (solved at 19) finished in exactly 8. symmetry false: no twin-switch flow-equality rows and no switch 'inflow == max(outs)' rule. Both restrict the model (neither is exact for a MILP), and the second costs a gp.max_ per copying-switch row. chunk_symmetry_breaking (default on) orders a host's interchangeable chunks instead, which is exact. See teccl/hierarchy/milp_design.md and teccl/ncclize/multicast_output_design.md.
